paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The Teacher looks at life "under the sun," and he says the same thing twice, loud: "Futility of futilities!" (Ecclesiastes 1:2). He asks what a man gains "from all his labor" (Ecclesiastes 1:3), and he doesn't have a quick answer. I think he wants you to stop and feel how big that question is.

Notice what he points at. The sun, the wind and the rivers keep going round and round, and "there is nothing new under the sun" (Ecclesiastes 1:9). Then he says "There is no remembrance of those who came before" (Ecclesiastes 1:11). So if we build our lives only on our own work and our own name, we're stamping dough that never finishes the batch. That's the weight of this passage, and I think it's meant to be heavy.

Here's why it matters to you. This honest look at life is one the Teacher is asking you to take, so you don't pin all your hope on things that go round and round. I bake every day, and I LOVE it, but even my best cookie gets eaten and gone by lunch. So hold your work, your plans and your name loosely, friend. This story isn't over, and the Teacher still has more to say.
